ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic Ordered to Pay $1.5 Billion in Largest AI Copyright Settlement
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic has been ordered to pay $1.5 billion in what is described as the largest AI copyright settlement to date, resolving a lawsuit over the use of pirated books to train its Claude AI model. The settlement has drawn attention in Europe as a signal of the financial stakes in AI training copyright disputes. Authors have expressed mixed reactions to the outcome.

ip_top_stories.title: COPYRIGHT NEWS—High Court of Delhi: AI training found to be fair use (Jul 27, 2026)
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that AI training on copyrighted content constitutes fair use, declining to grant an interim injunction sought by Indian news agency ANI against OpenAI. The court applied a threefold test and found that neither AI training nor ChatGPT outputs prima facie infringe copyright, marking India's first substantive judicial engagement with AI and copyright law. The ruling shifts the focus of India's AI copyright debate from training data to model outputs.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's $1.5bn copyright settlement approved, but AI training legal battles continue
ip_top_stories.summary: A detailed report on the approval of Anthropic's $1.5 billion copyright settlement notes that broader legal battles over AI training data remain unresolved. The settlement covers claims related to the use of pirated books but does not establish binding precedent for the wider industry.

ip_top_stories.title: GEMA, Suno ruling to test copyright limits for AI music training in Germany
ip_top_stories.summary: A legal case between German music rights organisation GEMA and AI music generator Suno is set to test the boundaries of copyright law as applied to AI training data in Germany. The outcome could have significant implications for how European courts interpret AI training and copyright, particularly in the music sector.

ip_top_stories.title: Artist sues AI meme generator for selling deeply personal comic as ad template
ip_top_stories.summary: An artist has filed a lawsuit against an AI meme generator after the platform used her deeply personal comic as an advertising template without authorisation. The case highlights concerns about AI tools scraping and commercialising creative works without the creator's consent.

ip_further_links.title: Authors have mixed feelings about the $1.5B Anthropic copyright infringement ruling
ip_further_links.summary: Authors respond with divided opinions to the $1.5 billion Anthropic settlement, with some welcoming the payout as recognition of harm and others questioning whether it sets a meaningful precedent for the broader creative community.

ip_further_links.title: Delhi HC's Threefold Test for AI Training: Why ANI Failed to Stop OpenAI's Use of Its News Content
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the Delhi High Court's threefold test applied in the ANI vs OpenAI case, explaining the legal reasoning behind the court's refusal to grant an injunction against ChatGPT's use of news content for training.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI ruling shifts India's AI copyright fight from training to outputs
ip_further_links.summary: Following the Delhi High Court's decision in the ANI vs OpenAI case, commentary argues the ruling reframes India's AI copyright debate away from training data and towards the outputs generated by AI systems.

ip_further_links.title: Harry Potter publisher secures major payout in historic AI copyright case
ip_further_links.summary: The publisher of the Harry Potter series has secured a significant financial payout in a landmark AI copyright case, adding to the growing body of settlements involving major publishers and AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Anthropic settles for $1.5 billion after training Claude on pirated books, and Europe is watching closely
ip_further_links.summary: Reporting on the Anthropic settlement notes that European regulators and publishers are closely monitoring the outcome as a potential benchmark for how AI training on copyrighted material should be compensated.

ip_further_links.title: Dog Photographer Loses Copyright Case Over AI-Generated Comic Version of Her Photo
ip_further_links.summary: A photographer has lost a copyright case after an AI-generated comic adaptation of her photograph was found not to infringe her rights, raising questions about the boundaries of copyright protection for AI-transformed works.

ip_further_links.title: WIPO Data Shows China's Generative AI Patent Surge Outpacing the World
ip_further_links.summary: New WIPO data reveals that China's generative AI patent filings are growing faster than any other country, indicating a significant shift in the global landscape of AI intellectual property ownership.

ip_further_links.title: Cosynd Expands Copyright Protection Platform to Defend Journalism's Value in the AI Era
ip_further_links.summary: Copyright protection platform Cosynd has announced an expansion of its services aimed at helping journalists and publishers protect their content from unauthorised AI ingestion and assert their rights in the AI era.

ip_further_links.title: Can Bangladesh's copyright law keep up with AI?
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis examines whether Bangladesh's existing copyright framework is adequate to address the challenges posed by AI-generated content and the use of copyrighted material in AI training.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT no longer mimics famous authors' writing styles: Report
ip_further_links.summary: Reports indicate that OpenAI has modified ChatGPT so that it no longer replicates the writing styles of well-known authors, a change that follows ongoing copyright pressure from the publishing community.
